A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IRG-MotionLLM and retain the same central method and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanML3D and KIT-ML experiments, training ablations, motion-captioning results, robustness tests and AToM reward-model experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds training-scale experiments, additional controls, MotionFix editing results and a four-participant user study.

M1.justification: The VQ-based architecture, eight Stage-1 tasks, Stage-2 intermediate-motion loss masking, three GRPO rewards and iterative refinement procedure are retained. MotionFix adaptation is described as additional fine-tuning, without specifying a new architecture, objective or refinement algorithm. Annotation filtering was already documented in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on MotionFix for text-guided motion editing (Appendix F.8), extending the experimentally demonstrated task coverage. HumanML3D, KIT-ML, InstructMotion-derived training data and AToM-general remain. Motion captioning was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 adds UniMo to GRPO comparisons, SALAD to the broader benchmark table, and MoMask+DisCoRD and Light-T2M to the alternative-evaluator comparison. Table 11 introduces two multi-agent pipelines; Table 14 adds editing comparisons against TMED and fine-tuned MotionLLM. The GPT4Vision label in Table 13 conflicts with retained GPT-4o prose, so that relabeling alone does not establish a different evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds a larger-data Stage-3 variant trained for 2,600 steps while retaining the original 900-step setting. New protocols include MotionFix fine-tuning and generated-target retrieval, random-position trajectory perturbations, and human evaluation using four participants, 80 prompts, 120 refinement pairs and 50 initial-final pairs. These are additional experimental settings, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test annotation filtering (Table 9), unified versus independently trained assessment/refinement experts (Table 11), increased GRPO training scale (Table 5), and perturbations beyond the first generated motion (Table 12). Appendix F.9 adds human assessments of naturalness and refinement effectiveness. Earlier refinement-round sensitivity, first-position perturbation tests and qualitative failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 evaluation repetitions and report 95% confidence intervals in benchmark comparisons. Additional interval-bearing rows follow the existing practice. The new user study reports averages and rates without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, agreement estimates or new seed-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Original headline scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added. The additional larger-data, 2,600-step model reports HumanML3D Top-1 0.564 and FID 0.208, versus the retained default model's 0.535 and 0.242 under different training conditions. MotionFix R@1 is 45.3 for the adapted model versus 39.3 for adapted MotionLLM. New human comparisons report 60% wins, 28% ties and 12% losses. Stage-1/2 reward-model rows and robustness Top-2 entries are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the reversed indexed ordering statement: v1 says m1 is more aligned than m2, whereas v2 says m2 is more aligned than m1, resolving its inconsistency with progressively improving trajectories. The reward definitions, VQ-VAE and GRPO equations remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows bidirectional knowledge flow to transfer from motion understanding to generation and emphasizes text-motion alignment rather than general generation performance. The introduction adds a contribution concerning adaptation to motion editing. The central claims about IRMoGen and three-stage training remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking joint training to better assessment/refinement and fewer parameters than multi-agent alternatives. Human ratings support a new distinction between worsened FID and preserved perceived naturalness, while qualifying refinement as beneficial but fallible. Appendix G additionally distinguishes demonstrated editing adaptation from still-unexplored interleaved reasoning for broader tasks. Earlier architectural and physical-realism limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds inference costs of 1.8–4.7 TFLOPs across zero to four refinement rounds, explicit manual-filtering examples and details of the new comparison setups. Conversely, it removes v1's explanation of generating a separate negative-pair set for Stage-2 and the Stage-1 reward-scoring recipe. Core hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged; the access statement changes from code/data to code/models.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted positioning against MotionFix's data construction and UniMo's GRPO training scale, alongside citations to SALAD, DisCoRD and newer motion models. These extend the research context without replacing the related-work taxonomy or the central positioning around a native generation-assessment-refinement loop.

P1.justification: Terminology changes from UniMoLM to MoLLM, the abstract and selected interpretations are revised, and affiliation text, keywords and acknowledgements change. Motion-captioning comparisons move from the appendix into Section 5.3, and appendix sections are reorganized and lettered. Much of the existing prose and overall narrative sequence is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column format, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. Five new tables present scaling, filtering, multi-agent, editing and user-study experiments. The robustness table gains a perturbation-position column and loses Top-2, while the reward table is shortened. Existing qualitative figures are largely preserved and redistributed.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens an already substantial empirical case through the unified-versus-expert control, human assessments of naturalness and refinement, and MotionFix transfer results. These provide useful checks beyond v1's automatic metrics and existing ablations. The gains outweigh the removed stage-specific reward results and annotation details, but remain incremental: the central method and matched benchmark results are unchanged, the human study has only four participants without uncertainty estimates, and the reward-baseline naming inconsistency remains unresolved.
